Local projections

Source: R/lp.R
lp.Rd

Jorda (2005) local projections: for each horizon \(h=0,\dots,H\) and each response \(y_k\), $$y_{k,t+h} = \alpha_h + \beta_h s_t + \gamma_h' w_t + e_{t+h},$$ where \(s_t\) is the shock, \(w_t\) the controls (lags of Y, optional contemporaneous variables, extra controls). \(\beta_h\) is the impulse response at horizon \(h\). The regressions, 2SLS and HAC standard errors run in C++.

Usage

lp(
  Y,
  shock,
  horizon = 20L,
  lags = 4L,
  contemp = NULL,
  controls = NULL,
  iv = NULL,
  responses = NULL,
  cumulative = NULL,
  se = c("nw", "hc"),
  nw_lag = NULL,
  lag_augment = FALSE,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9),
  dof_adjust = FALSE
)

Arguments

Y

data frame / tibble / matrix (T x K) of responses (and the source of lag controls). Non-numeric columns (e.g. a date) are dropped.

shock

the shock \(s_t\): a variable of Y (tidyselect; observed shock, unit-impact normalisation) or a numeric vector of length T (external shock series, e.g. narrative).

horizon

maximum horizon H.

lags

number of lags of Y in the controls (and of an external shock).

contemp

<tidy-select> variables of Y entered contemporaneously as controls. For a recursive (Cholesky) identification with shock a variable of Y, list the variables ordered before the shock.

controls

optional extra T x q matrix of controls.

iv

optional T x q matrix of instruments for shock (LP-IV; Stock & Watson 2018).

responses

<tidy-select> responses to use (default all variables of Y).

cumulative

<tidy-select> variables whose response is cumulated (\(\sum_{j=0}^h y_{t+j}\)), for variables measured in differences.

se

"nw" Newey-West/Bartlett or "hc" Eicker-Huber-White (HC1).

nw_lag

Newey-West truncation lag; default h + 1.

lag_augment

Montiel Olea & Plagborg-Moller (2021) lag augmentation: add one extra lag that is not interpreted and use "hc" standard errors, valid without stationarity assumptions and robust at long horizons.

level

confidence levels for the pointwise bands.

dof_adjust

apply an n/(n-m) small-sample factor to the Newey-West variance.

Value

an lpm object: $estimate ((H+1) x K), $se, $bands, $nobs. Use tidy() for a tibble and autoplot() for a ggplot.

See also

Other local projections: autoplot.lpm(), compare_lp_var(), lp_forecast(), lp_joint(), lp_panel(), lp_smooth(), lp_state(), lp_supt(), tidy.lpm()

Examples

fit <- lp(yraw, shock = rate, horizon = 12, lags = 2, contemp = c(infl, unemp))
fit
#> <lpm> local projection of infl, unemp, rate on 'rate', horizons 0..12 (2 lags, NW)
#>       infl   unemp    rate
#> 0   0.0000  0.0000  1.0000
#> 1  -0.0589 -0.0295  0.7650
#> 4  -0.0217  0.0284  0.5960
#> 8  -0.0745  0.1937  0.1735
#> 12 -0.4550  0.1486 -0.1578
tidy(fit)
#> # A tibble: 78 × 7
#>    horizon response  estimate std.error level  conf.low conf.high
#>      <int> <fct>        <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>

#>  2       1 infl     -5.89e- 2  4.20e- 2   0.9 -1.28e- 1  1.01e- 2
#>  3       2 infl     -6.16e- 2  7.23e- 2   0.9 -1.81e- 1  5.74e- 2
#>  4       3 infl     -3.15e- 2  1.05e- 1   0.9 -2.04e- 1  1.41e- 1
#>  5       4 infl     -2.17e- 2  1.52e- 1   0.9 -2.72e- 1  2.28e- 1
#>  6       5 infl     -7.74e- 3  1.71e- 1   0.9 -2.88e- 1  2.73e- 1
#>  7       6 infl     -1.53e- 2  1.79e- 1   0.9 -3.10e- 1  2.79e- 1
